key_results: I re-read the earlier run's unverified work (commits daeb5ba, a9a1b70, 667f153) against the code and re-ran everything. The well-conditioned root finder in solver/src/mermin.rs is mathematically correct. It writes sum g f - N exactly as P - Hl - d about a split of the levels, computes the hole factors as f(-x) and never as 1 - f, and comes in two forms: LogBalance (canonical, log domain, Newton then bisection down to adjacent doubles) and LinearDeviation (refined run, plain bisection). In all 135 thermal states mu is its own form's root bit for bit.

One fix to that work: the earlier rounding bound left out the rounding of the arguments x_i = (eps_i - mu)/T and the extra errors of the log domain. I re-derived it to first order. It is now eps_mach[(n+2+L)(P+Hl+|d|)/(dN/dmu) + 3<|eps-mu|> + T(ln g_max+3) + 2|mu|], where L is the larger |ln| of the two sides of the balance and the mean is weighted with g f(1-f). The 40-digit tool evaluates the same bound on its own, at the 40-digit root.

Against roots I computed independently with mpmath at 40 digits: the solver's mu is within the bound in 135 of 135 states. The largest error is 2.433e-16 m (N136_lamp1_a20_T50), the largest ratio to the bound is 0.149, and for N8_lamm1_a00_T10 the error is -2.519e-17 m against a bound of 3.154e-16. The old direct count misses that root by 8.267e-10 m.

The Rust unit test forty_digit_roots and the solver check thermo_mu_vs_40digit_roots pass on the 8 worst states (fixture sha256 edfa5584ddc83655; largest ratio 0.124; the old direct count's error is 2.3e6 times the largest new bound). The solver check thermo_mu_well_conditioned_root also passes (max ratio 0.318, largest bound 4.77e-14 m). Solver report: 42/42.

Re-runs: the canonical matrix and its repeat give all 244 result files and the report byte-identical. The refined run passes; ks-rust-determinism.json is 14/14. Only the thermal outputs changed. Ground, excited, adiabatic, spectrum, rescaling and exact-Fock files are byte-identical to 70fab64, apart from the history label line in adiabatic/history.json.

How the uncertainty measure was made sensitive to the root's rounding error. (1) The canonical run uses LogBalance and the refined run uses LinearDeviation (also `single --refined`, which the checker uses), so the root's rounding error enters |mu_c - mu_r| instead of cancelling. (2) Each run's bound is added: U_mu = |mu_c - mu_r| + B_c + B_r (max 1.255e-12 m), U_Omega = |Omega_c - Omega_r| + N(B_c + B_r) (max 2.753e-10). (3) A new column, mu_direct_count_minus_mu, drives a live negative control in refined_mermin_root_path. For N8_lamm1_a00_T10 the old measure (direct count in both runs) is 5.8e-16 m against an actual error of 8.267e-10 m: blind. The new refined run differs from an old-style canonical root by 8.271e-10 m, so it would catch it. N8_lam0_a00_T10 and N8_lamp1_a00_T10 behave the same way.

findings.evidence: Numerical check with Revision/algebra/gammas.json and h_m(k) = -i m gamma^(x4) - gamma^(x4) sum k_a gamma^a. At (m, k) = (0, 0): rank 0, kernel dimension 16, eigenvalues of B on the kernel from -1 to +1 (inertia (8,8)). At (0, k1 = k5 = 1) and (1, k5 = 1): rank 8, kernel dimension 8, B identically zero on the kernel. Theorem Q has no hypothesis m != 0 or (m, k) != (0, 0). verify_pairing.wls line 351 tests `MatrixRank[h] == 8` only on the samples. A general argument exists: for m != 0, N = i m + kslash satisfies gamma4 N gamma4^-1 = -(-i m + kslash) and N + (-i m + kslash) = 2 kslash is invertible, so rank N = 8. For m = 0 a nonzero null kslash has rank 8.
